s: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga. Whose commander was he?
x: Panduranga, the commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, issued the Addanki inscription.

s: Which title was assumed by Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III took the title Tripura Martya Maheshwara. Kollabhiganda was Vijayaditya IV, Rajamahendra Ammaraja I and Vishamasiddhi Kubja Vishnuvardhana.

s: Gunaga Vijayaditya III's victories over Kiranapuram and Achalapuram are linked with which of his titles?
x: The title Tripura Martya Maheshwara marks Gunaga Vijayaditya III's victories over three cities, including Kiranapuram and Achalapuram.

s:
Consider the following statements about Gunaga Vijayaditya III:
1. He is regarded as the greatest king of the Eastern Chalukyas.
2. His commander Pandaranga issued the Addanki inscription.
3. He made Rajamahendravaram his capital.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III was the greatest Eastern Chalukya king and Pandaranga was his commander. Rajamahendravaram was made capital by Ammaraja I.

s: Which town did Gunaga Vijayaditya III develop as another Bejawada?
x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III developed Kandukuru (Kandukur) on the model of Bejawada.

s: What was the major cultural contribution of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They confined literary activity exclusively to Sanskrit.
They ended the use of Telugu in the Vengi region.
They turned Telugu into a literary language.
They replaced Telugu with Tamil as the court language.
x: A major significance of the Eastern Chalukyas was that they helped turn Telugu into a literary language and laid the foundation for Telugu literature.

s: Who had the title 'Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara'?
x: Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara was Narayana Bhattu's title; Nannaya was known as Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.

s: The Porumamilla inscription is related to which person?
x: The Porumamilla tank inscription, which lays down 12 rules for tank construction, is associated with Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura. Rudrapurushadatta was an Ikshvaku king and Dhananjaya Varma issued the Kalamalla inscription.

s: Regarding the Nandampudi inscription, which of the following is correct?
o: Nannaya composed it and Narayana Bhattu received the agrahara
Narayana Bhattu composed it and Nannaya received the agrahara
Pandaranga composed it and Nannaya received the agrahara
Nannaya composed it and Ugradityacharya received the agrahara
x: Nannaya composed the Nandampudi inscription of Rajaraja Narendra, and the agrahara was given to his collaborator Narayana Bhattu (G2 2017 key). Pandaranga is linked to the Addanki inscription and Ugradityacharya to Kalyanakaraka.

s: Why is the Addanki inscription notable?
o: Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription
Chalukya Bhima I's military victory at Peruvanguru
Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu
x: The Addanki inscription is associated with Pandaranga, the general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, and is regarded as the first Telugu verse inscription.

s: Which is the earliest Telugu inscription of the pre-Nannaya period?
x: The Kalamalla inscription, dated approximately to 575 CE and associated with Renati Choda Dhananjaya, predates Nannaya.

s: To which ruler do the Korumelli plates, written by the same scribe as the Nandampudi inscription, belong?
x: The Korumelli plates and the Nandampudi inscription both belong to Rajaraja Narendra.

s: How many rules for tank construction does the Porumamilla inscription lay down?
x: The Porumamilla inscription of prince Bhaskara Bhavadura gives 12 rules for tank construction.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler issued the Magallu inscription, the first to mention the Kakatiyas?
x: The Magallu inscription of Danarnava is the first record to mention the Kakatiyas.

s: In which metre is the Addanki inscription, the first Telugu verse inscription, composed?
x: Pandaranga's Addanki inscription is in the Taruvoja metre.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajaraja Narendra ruled from Rajamahendravaram.
2. Rajaraja Narendra himself began the Telugu Mahabharata translation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Rajaraja Narendra ruled from Rajamahendravaram; it was his court poet Nannaya who began the Telugu Mahabharata, with the king as patron.

s: Why is Nannaya Bhattaraka regarded as the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature?
o: composed the first Telugu literary work, Andhra Mahabharatamu
founded the first Telugu literary academy at Vengi
translated the complete Ramayana into Telugu
introduced the prose style into Sanskrit literature
x: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as Adi Kavi because Andhra Mahabharatamu is considered the first major Telugu literary work.

s: Andhra Mahabharatamu of Nannaya is written in which literary style?
o: Champu style combining verse and prose
x: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu follows the Champu style, which combines verse and prose.

s: Pavuluri Ganitamu, the first scientific text in Telugu, is a verse rendering of which work?
x: Pavuluri Ganitamu renders Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham in Telugu verse. Kalyanakaraka is a medical work, Kavijanasrayam a work of Vemulavada Bhimakavi, and Andhra Mahabharatamu the first Telugu literary work.

s: Who wrote 'Kavijanasrayam'?
x: Kavijanasrayam is Vemulavada Bhimakavi's work; Ugradityacharya wrote Kalyanakaraka and Pavuluri Mallana the Pavuluri Ganitamu.

s: Who had the titles 'Vagadheeshwara' and 'Shabda Shasanudu'?
x: Nannaya bore the titles Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu; Narayana Bhattu was Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara.

s: Who was the court poet of Rajaraja Narendra who began the Andhra Mahabharatamu?
x: Nannaya Bhattaraka, court poet of Rajaraja Narendra, began the Andhra Mahabharatamu.

s: Which of the following inscription – significance pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Magallu – first inscription to mention the Kakatiyas
Magallu – first inscription to mention the Gajapatis
x: The Magallu inscription is noted as the first inscription mentioning the Kakatiyas, not the Gajapatis; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which region formed Venginadu, the core territory of the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The core territory was the Krishna-Godavari doab (Venginadu), with capitals at Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry.

s: Who shifted the capital of the Eastern Chalukyas to Vengi?
x: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Vengi, identified with Pedavegi.

s: Arrange the capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas in chronological order:
x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana ruled from Pithapuram, Jayasimha Vallabha I moved to Vengi, and Rajamahendravaram is linked with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra.

s: By what name is Vengi referred to in Dandin's Dashakumaracharita?
x: Dandin calls Vengi 'Andhra Nagaram'. Mangalapura is Mangalagiri in the Kopparam inscription, Pishtapura is Pithapuram, and Rajamahendra is a title of Ammaraja I.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Marturu inscription refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura.
2. The Vipparla inscription was issued by Jayasimha Vallabha.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Marturu inscription calls Mangalagiri Mangalapura, and the Vipparla inscription was issued by the Eastern Chalukya Jayasimha Vallabha.

s: After whom did Bezawada take the name Vijayawada?
x: Bezawada came to be called Vijayawada after Vijayaditya.

s: From which royal title did Rajahmundry get its name?
x: Ammaraja I bore the title Rajamahendra; Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) is named after it.

s: Which city became the third capital of the Eastern Chalukyas, after Pithapuram and Vengi?
x: The capitals moved from Pithapuram to Vengi and then to Rajamahendravaram, which Ammaraja I made the capital.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram the capital of the Eastern Chalukyas.
2. Rajaraja Narendra ruled from Rajahmundry and made it famous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram the capital, and Rajaraja Narendra later ruled from it and made it famous.

s: With which present place is Vengi, the second capital of the Eastern Chalukyas, identified?
x: Vengi is Pedavegi near Eluru; Jayasimha I shifted the capital there from Pithapuram.

s: In which year did Kubja Vishnuvardhana declare his independence and found the Eastern Chalukya line?
x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana became viceroy in 617 CE and declared independence in 624 CE.

s: What was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
x: The boar, or Varaha, was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas.

s: Which other dynasties also used the matronymic 'Hariti-putra', like the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The matronymic Hariti-putra was also used by the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas, indicating a southern cultural connection.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi:
1. Sanskrit was their official language.
2. Most of their about 100 donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit.
3. Kannada was their official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sanskrit was the official language and most of the about 100 donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit. Kannada was not their official language, so 3 is wrong.

s: After 973 CE, who was the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: After 973 CE, the Kalyani Chalukyas emerged as the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas. Satyasraya and Someshvara I are associated with this later phase.

s: During which period did the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi rule?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled approximately from 624 to 1075 CE; 1076-1210 belongs to the Chalukya-Chola phase.

s:
Assertion (A): The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas.
Reason (R): Kubja Vishnuvardhana, the first Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi, was the brother of Pulakeshin II.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true: the Eastern Chalukyas branched from the Badami line because Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Pulakeshin II's brother, founded their rule in Vengi.

s: What was 'Tribhuvanankusa', found on Eastern Chalukya copper-plate seals?
x: Tribhuvanankusa was the seal sign manual on Eastern Chalukya copper-plate seals. The royal emblem was the boar, the matronymic was Hariti-putra and the mother goddess was Hariti.

s: By defeating which dynasty did Pulakeshin II take the Vengi region (c. 616 CE)?
x: Pulakeshin II took the Krishna-Godavari region (Vengi) after defeating the remnants of the Vishnukundins.

s: Who was the last king of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
x: Vijayaditya VII (1070-1075) was the last king; his death in 1075 ended the Vengi line.

s: In which year was Kubja Vishnuvardhana made viceroy of Vengi by Pulakeshin II?
x: Kubja was made viceroy in 617 CE and declared independence in 624 CE.

s: How do the Kopparam copper plates (631 CE) of Pulakeshin II refer to Kubja Vishnuvardhana?
x: The Kopparam plates of 631 CE call Kubja Vishnuvardhana 'Yuvaraja' and record the conquest of the Krishna-Godavari region.

s: In which regnal year of Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the grant recorded in the Chipurupalli plates made?
x: The Chipurupalli plates (632 CE) record Kubja's grant in his 18th regnal year and name the scholar Madhavasharma.

s: Which of the following was a title of Kubja Vishnuvardhana?
x: Besides Vishamasiddhi, Kubja Vishnuvardhana had the titles Sarvasiddhi and Makaradhwaja.

s: In which present district were the Chipurupalli plates of Kubja Vishnuvardhana found?
x: The Chipurupalli (Cheepurupalli) plates, a grant of Kubja's 18th regnal year, are from Vizianagaram.

s: Which of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Chalukya Chandra was the title of Saktivarma I, not Vimaladitya. Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima.

s: 'Rajamartanda' was a title of which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
x: Rajamartanda (also Mummadi Bhima) was a title of Vimaladitya. Saktivarma I was Chalukya Chandra, Rajaraja Narendra was Rajarajanarayana, and Kollabhiganda was Vijayaditya IV, not Chalukya Bhima.

s: According to the Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva, Chalukya Bhima I fought how many battles?
x: The Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva credits Chalukya Bhima I, who ruled 30 years and built the Pancharamas, with 360 battles.

s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.

s: In which year was the Eastern Chalukya ruler Rajaraja Narendra crowned?
x: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned on 16 August 1022. In 1006 Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi (sent by Satyasraya), and in 1070 Vijayaditya VII ousted Rajendra Chalukya.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler held the title Kollabhiganda, ruled only about six months and died in the battle of Virajapuri?
x: Vijayaditya IV, eldest son of Chalukya Bhima I, ruled about six months and died at Virajapuri invading Kalinga.

s: Who had the title 'Chalukya Chandra'?
x: Chalukya Chandra was Saktivarma I's title; Vimaladitya was Rajamartanda and Ammaraja I Rajamahendra.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler had the title 'Kavyageetha Priyudu'?
x: Rajaraja Narendra, the patron of Nannaya, was called Kavyageetha Priyudu.

s: Who among the following had the title 'Samasta Bhuvanashraya'?
x: Samasta Bhuvanashraya was the title of Jayasimha I (Jayasimha Vallabha), who shifted the capital to Vengi.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Title)
A. Samasta Bhuvanashraya
B. Rajamartanda
C. Chalukya Chandra
D. Kollabhiganda
List-II (Ruler)
1. Saktivarma I
2. Vijayaditya IV
3. Jayasimha I
4. Vimaladitya
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Samasta Bhuvanashraya - Jayasimha I; Rajamartanda - Vimaladitya; Chalukya Chandra - Saktivarma I; Kollabhiganda - Vijayaditya IV.

s: Kokkili, from whom Vishnuvardhana III took back the throne, set up which kingdom?
x: Kokkili set up the Yalamanchili kingdom; Vishnuvardhana III took the throne back from him.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Chalukya Bhima I fought Krishna II, not Dhruva. Vijayaditya II fought the Rashtrakutas under Amoghavarsha, while Gunaga Vijayaditya defeated Krishna II and the Kalinga king Devendravarma.

s: Which daughter of Vishnuvardhana IV did the Rashtrakuta Dhruva marry after defeating him?
x: Vishnuvardhana IV, who backed Govinda III, was defeated by Dhruva, who then married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi.

s: Where did Chalukya Bhima I repel the forces of Rashtrakuta Krishna II?
x: Chalukya Bhima I repelled Krishna II's forces at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru.

s: Under which Eastern Chalukya ruler did the conflict with Dantidurga, founder of the Rashtrakutas, begin?
x: The conflict with Dantidurga began under Vijayaditya I; Vengi had helped the Badami line that Dantidurga ended.

s: By what name was Kulottunga I, who united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines, earlier known?
x: Kulottunga I was Rajendra Chalukya, who united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines.

s: Who seized Vengi after killing Danarnava during the interlude in Eastern Chalukya history?
x: The Telugu Choda ruler Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and seized Vengi until Danarnava’s sons recovered it with Chola assistance.

s: Who supported Rajaraja Narendra in his succession war against Vijayaditya VII?
x: Rajaraja Narendra, the son of Kundavva, was supported by Rajendra I. Vijayaditya VII, the son of Melama, was supported by Kalyani Jayasimha II.

s: At Koppam in 1053, who killed Rajadhiraja I?
x: Ahavamalla Someshwara killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam in 1053. Rajadhiraja had earlier won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka.

s: Who ousted Vijayaditya VII, the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukyas, in 1070 CE?
o: Rajendra Chalukya, later known as Kulottunga I
x: Rajendra Chalukya ousted Vijayaditya VII in 1070 CE and later became known as Kulottunga I.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vimaladitya — Kundavva, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I
2. Vimaladitya — Melama, daughter of Jatachoda Bhima
3. Rajaraja Narendra — Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
x: All three pairs are correct. Vimaladitya married both Kundavva and Melama, while Rajaraja Narendra married Ammanga Devi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola.

s: Rajaraja Narendra married Ammanga Devi. Whose daughter was she?
x: Rajaraja Narendra married Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola; Kundavva, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I, was his mother.

s: In which year was Vimaladitya, husband of the Chola princess Kundavva, crowned?
x: Vimaladitya was crowned in May 1011; 1006 was Saktivarma I's victory over Bayyalanambi and 1022 Rajaraja Narendra's coronation.

s: Kulottunga I married Madhurantaki. Whose daughter was she?
x: Madhurantaki, daughter of the Chola Rajendra II, married Kulottunga I (Rajendra Chalukya).

s: Who among the following married Madhurantaki, the Chola princess?
x: Vimaladitya married Kundavai, while Kulottunga I married Madhurantaki.

s: Which Chola king won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka?
x: Rajadhiraja I won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka, but he was killed at Koppam in 1053.

s: After the battle of Koppam (1053), whose suzerainty did Rajaraja Narendra have to accept?
x: After Ahavamalla Someshwara killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam, Rajaraja Narendra had to accept Kalyani suzerainty.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler issued the Chekurru copper plate?
x: The Chekurru copper plate belongs to Ammaraja I, who made Rajamahendravaram the capital.

s: Who issued the Kopparam copper plates of 631 CE?
x: The Kopparam plates are a record of Pulakeshin II; they call Kubja 'Yuvaraja'.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas called themselves Haritiputras and their mother goddess was Hariti (APPSC G2 2019); Kushmandini is a Jain yakshi. Kalyanakaraka is Ugradityacharya's medical work, not a Shaiva school.

s: Who was the court singer and dancer of Chalukya Bhima I?
x: Chellavva was the court singer and dancer of Chalukya Bhima I. Chamekamba was a courtesan linked with Ammaraja II.

s: Which title did Chellavva, the court singer of Chalukya Bhima I, hold?
x: Chellavva held the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada (also Samasta Gandharva Vidyakovida).

s:
Arrange the following Andhra dynasties in chronological order:
1. Kakatiyas
2. Eastern Chalukyas
3. Vijayanagara
4. Reddis
x: Eastern Chalukyas (624–1075) came first, then the Kakatiyas (1163–1323), the Reddis and Vijayanagara.

s: By what name is the Chalukya-Chola era in Andhra (1076–c.1210), the age of the Velanati Chodas, also known?
x: The Chalukya-Chola phase of 1076–c.1210 is known as the Mandalika Yugam, before the Kakatiyas (1163–1323) rose.

s: Who built the Kesari Samudra lake (Kesamudram)?
x: The Kesari Samudra lake was built by the Kakatiya Prola I, not Rudradeva.

s: Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram is associated with which ruler?
x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler granted Mushikonda village to the Jains?
x: Vishnuvardhana III patronised Vedic and Jain faiths and granted Mushikonda village to the Jains.

s: Who issued the Maliyapundi grant to a Jain temple at Dharmapuri?
x: Ammaraja II issued the Maliyapundi grant at the request of his vassal Durgaraja.

s: Which grant records Queen Ayyana Mahadevi's Nedumba Vasati?
x: The Musinikonda grant of Vishnuvardhana III records Ayyana Mahadevi's Nedumba Vasati.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Vengi school of Eastern Chalukya architecture)?
o: Name of the style – Vesara or Chalukya
Vimana – Dravidian form with Buddhist influence
Base of the temple – raised jagati
x: The Vengi school used local sandstone, not granite; the Vesara/Chalukya name, Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence and raised jagati are correct.

s: Which group of temples at Bikkavolu is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temples of Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara and Chandrashekhara are attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.

s: Who built the Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot?
x: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot, also called Chalukya Bhimavaram, are associated with Chalukya Bhima I.

s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.

s: Who among the following is associated with the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple?
x: Chamekamba, a courtesan during the reign of Ammaraja II, secured the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple.

s: Ayyana Mahadevi built the Jain Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati near Vijayawada. Whose queen was she?
x: The standard view (Musinikonda grant) makes Ayyana Mahadevi the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana; note that the APPSC 2025 key gave Gunaga Vijayaditya III. Ammaraja II is linked to Chamekamba and the Kaluchumbarru grant, and Vimaladitya married Kundavai.

s: Which faith was dominant under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
x: Shaivism was dominant; the dynasty was tolerant and also patronised Jainism and Buddhism.

s: Who built three Shiva temples at Kalidindi for fallen Chola soldiers?
x: Rajaraja Narendra built three Shiva temples at Kalidindi for fallen Chola soldiers.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Temple)
A. 108 Saiva temples
B. Pancharamas
C. Kunti Madhava temple, Pithapuram
D. Kartikeya temple, Bezawada
List-II (Builder)
1. Kubja Vishnuvardhana
2. Vijayaditya II
3. Yuddhamalla
4. Chalukya Bhima I
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Vijayaditya II built the 108 Saiva temples, Chalukya Bhima I the Pancharamas, Kubja Vishnuvardhana the Kunti Madhava temple and Yuddhamalla the Kartikeya temple at Bezawada.

s: Why did Vijayaditya II build 108 Saiva temples?
o: To mark his coronation at Vengi
For the Chola soldiers who fell in war
To celebrate his victory over the Kalyani Chalukyas
x: Vijayaditya II fought 108 battles in 12 years and built 108 Saiva temples as penance. The Kalidindi temples for fallen Chola soldiers were Rajaraja Narendra's.

s: Vijayaditya II is traditionally associated with which of the following achievements?
o: Winning 18 battles in one regnal year
x: Vijayaditya II is said to have fought 108 battles in 12 years. He built 108 Saiva temples as penance for these battles, as recorded in the Sataluru inscription.

s: Which inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with 108 temples?
x: The Sataluru inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with the 108 temples. Addanki is associated with Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription.

s: By what name were the 108 Saiva temples built by Vijayaditya II known?
x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) built 108 Saiva temples called Narendreswara or Narendra Mrigeswaralayas, recorded in the Sataluru inscription.

s: What was Hallisaka, identified with Kolatam?
x: Hallisaka, or Kolatam, was a popular dance associated with the cultural life of the period.

s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, who was Chellavva?
x: Musicians and dancers were attached to Eastern Chalukya temples and courts, and Chellavva is an example of such a court-linked singer and dancer.

s: Which statement about Panchadarla in Anakapalli is correct?
o: It contains the only two-flagpole temple in Andhra Pradesh.
Its inscriptions record the construction of the Ramappa vimana.
Its temple is exclusively a Kalinga-style monument of the Eastern Gangas.
Its Uma Dharmalingeswara Temple has Eastern Chalukya and fifteenth-century inscriptions.
x: The Uma Dharmalingeswara Temple at Panchadarla has Eastern Chalukya and fifteenth-century inscriptions.

s: Where are sculptures of musical instruments of this period found?
x: Sculptures of musical instruments are found at Bhairavakona.

s: For which of the following is Bhairavakona in the Nallamala hills known?
o: Eight rock-cut cave temples of Shiva
x: Bhairavakona has eight rock-cut cave temples of Shiva of about the 7th-8th century CE.

s: 'Kavigayaka Kalpataru' was the title of which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
x: Ammaraja II was Kavigayaka Kalpataru; Vishnuvardhana III was Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu and Rajaraja Narendra Kavyageetha Priyudu.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bhattavamana wrote Kavyalankara Sutras and held the title Kavi Vrishabha.

s: Which statement regarding Chellavva’s patronage is correct?
o: She was patronised by Vimaladitya, who granted her Mushikonda.
She was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I, who granted her Attili.
She was patronised by Danarnava, who granted her Pithapuram.
She was patronised by Rajaraja Narendra, who granted her Ramatirtham.
x: Chellavva was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I, who gave her Attili village and two kandikas of land.

s: Which title was held by Bhattavamana, author of the Kavyalankara Sutras?
x: Bhattavamana was Kavi Vrishabha; the other titles belonged to Vishnuvardhana III, Ammaraja II and Rajaraja Narendra.

s: Who had the title 'Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu'?
x: Vishnuvardhana III was Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu; Ammaraja II was Kavigayaka Kalpataru.

s: Chellavva of the Eastern Chalukya court is known by which title?
x: Chellavva, court singer of Chalukya Bhima I, had the title Gandharva-vidya-visarada. Kavi Vrishabha was Bhattavamana's title.

s: Who was the father of Chellavva, compared to Tumburu in the Attili inscription?
x: The Attili inscription compares Mallappa, Chellavva's father, to Tumburu.

s: What is the subject of Ugradityacharya's Kalyanakaraka?
x: Kalyanakaraka is a Jain Ayurvedic book on diagnosis and treatment, written by Ugradityacharya.

s: Ugradityacharya, author of the Kalyanakaraka, was a Jain scholar of which place?
x: Ugradityacharya was a Jain scholar of Ramatirtha.

s: In whose court was Bhattavamana, author of the Kavyalankara Sutras?
x: Bhattavamana (title Kavi Vrishabha) was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I.

s: Which development is associated with Jayasimha II?
o: The Boyas founded the merchant headquarters at Penugonda.
The Koya Kottalu were drawn into the Brahmanical fold.
The Venginadu was divided into eighteen offices.
x: Under Jayasimha II, groups such as the Koya Kottalu were assimilated into the Brahmanical fold.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have performed the Ashvamedha?
x: Jayasimha I performed the Ashvamedha, while royal prashastis also boast of several Ashvamedhas.

s: Which of the following were the Shaiva sects prevalent under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The Shaiva sects of the period were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata. Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are Vaishnava traditions, and Virashaiva persecution came later in the Kakatiya age.

s: Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa were traditions of which faith?
x: Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are Vaishnava traditions; the Shaiva sects were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata.

s: Which Vaishnava Eastern Chalukya ruler built the Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot?
x: Danarnava, a Vaishnava, built the Mandavya Narayana temple; Kubja Vishnuvardhana built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.

s: What were the Ashtadasa Tirthas in Eastern Chalukya administration?
x: The kingdom followed the Saptanga idea and had Ashtadasa Tirthas, meaning eighteen offices.

s: What was the council of ministers called under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The Eastern Chalukya council of ministers was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was its chief member.

s: Which of the following Nadus was associated with the Nellore region?
x: Pakanadu was associated with Nellore. Venginadu covered parts of Krishna and Godavari, while Kammanadu included Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vishaya or Mandala — Vishayapati or Mandaleswara
x: The state was organised into Vishayas or Mandalas under a Vishayapati or Mandaleswara.

s: Who were the Vanneyus under the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: Members of the council of ministers
x: Vanneyus collected tolls; Grameyaka/Urgavunda was the village head and the Sthanadhipati managed temples.

s: Who was the chief member of the Tirthulu (council of ministers) of the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The Samaharta was the chief of the Tirthulu; the Vishayapati/Mandaleswara headed a province and the Grameyaka a village.

s: Which region did Kammanadu of the Eastern Chalukya period cover?
x: Kammanadu covered Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet; Pakanadu was Nellore and Venginadu parts of Krishna and Godavari.

s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya administration:
1. Grameyaka or Urgavunda was the village head.
2. The Sthanadhipati collected tolls.
3. Ashtadasa Tirthas were the eighteen administrative offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. The Sthanadhipati managed temples and their land endowments; tolls were collected by the Vanneyus.

s: In Eastern Chalukya grants, Udranga was a tax on what?
x: Udranga is explained in epigraphy as the fixed or principal land tax (tax on permanent tenants), paired with uparikara; it was not a water tax.

s: How many limbs of the state does the Saptanga idea, followed by the Eastern Chalukyas, name?
x: Saptanga means seven limbs of the state; eighteen was the number of offices (Ashtadasa Tirthas).

s: Who was the king's adviser on judicial matters under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The Pradvivaka was the king's adviser on judicial matters (chief judge).

s: What were 'jayapatras' under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: Disputes were settled with local elders, and written verdicts were called jayapatras.

s: Which officer managed temples and their land endowments under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: The Sthanadhipati managed temples and their land endowments.

s: What were the Ashtadasha Tirthas in the Eastern Chalukya administration of Vengi?
x: The Ashtadasha Tirthas were the 18 departments; the Yuvaraja was a partner in governance and councils were called Varagoshti.

s: What were the councils of the Eastern Chalukya administration called?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas had 18 departments (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and councils called Varagoshti.

s: Brahmins who received agraharas are stated to have performed which rituals?
x: Brahmins receiving tax-free agraharas performed Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna rituals.

s: Who subdued the Boyas?
x: Panduranga subdued the Boyas, while Jayasimha II is associated with the assimilation of the Koya Kottalu.

s: Who were the Panchanamvaru, who appear as an organised body from the Eastern Chalukya period?
o: Five merchant guilds of the ports
x: Panchanamvaru were the five artisan groups: blacksmith, goldsmith, brazier, carpenter and sculptor.

s: Which inscription of Chalukya Bhima I names a Setti Shreshthi (chief merchant)?
x: Chalukya Bhima I's Kakumanu inscription names a Setti Shreshthi.

s: Who sent 72 merchants to China?
x: The 72-merchant mission to China is associated with Kulothunga I; Saktivarma's coins have been found in Arakan, Burma.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched (overseas trade under the Eastern Chalukyas)?
o: Coins found in Arakan (Burma) – Kulothunga I
72 merchants sent to China – Saktivarma I
Trade with the eastern islands – Rajaraja Narendra
Headquarters of the merchant guilds – Pithapuram
x: Rajaraja Narendra traded with the eastern islands; Arakan coins belong to Saktivarma I, the 72 merchants were sent by Kulothunga I, and the guild headquarters was Penugonda.

s: Which place was the headquarters of the merchant guilds in medieval Andhra?
x: Penugonda was the headquarters of the merchant guilds in medieval Andhra.

s: Coins of which Eastern Chalukya ruler have been found in Arakan (Burma)?
x: Coins of Saktivarma I found in Arakan show overseas trade.

s: During which period did the persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu take place?
x: The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred in the Kakatiya age, not under the Eastern Chalukyas, who patronised Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism.

s:
Consider the following statements about religion under the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Potlacheruvu was a famous Buddhist centre.
2. Vimaladitya was the only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain.
3. Amaravati was a centre where declining Buddhism survived.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Potlacheruvu was a famous Jain centre, not a Buddhist one.

s: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham for whom?
o: His Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva
x: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva, as recorded in the Ramateertham inscription.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mushikonda grant to Jains – Kubja Vishnuvardhana
x: Ammaraja II made the Kaluchumbarru grant at the request of Chamekamba; Mushikonda village was granted to Jains by Vishnuvardhana III.

s: At whose request did Ammaraja II renew the Maliyapundi gift to a Jinalaya near Dharmapuri?
x: The Maliyapundi grant was made at the request of the vassal Durgaraja; Chamekamba requested the Kaluchumbarru grant.

s: In which district is Ramatirtham, where Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple?
x: Ramatirtham, with the Jain Ramakonda cave temple, is in Vizianagaram district.

s: What were Ghatikas in the Eastern Chalukya period?
o: Military cantonments attached to royal forts
Jain cave temples used for royal burials
Advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples
Merchant guilds situated at coastal ports
x: Ghatikas were advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples.

s: Which of the following subjects was NOT included among the subjects taught in Ghatikas?
x: Ghatikas taught subjects such as Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda and Ayurveda. Hallisaka was a popular dance, not an academic subject.

s: What were the heads of Ghatikas called?
x: The heads of Ghatikas were called Ghatika Samanyulu.

s: Mandasharma was the head (Ghatika Samanyulu) of which Ghatika?
x: Mandasharma headed the Asanapura Ghatika in Kammanadu.

s: With which words did Jain pupils begin their studies in this period?
x: Jain pupils began their studies with 'Om Namah Siddham'.

s: Who built the twin Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot?
x: Chalukya Bhima I built the twin temples Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama Bhimeswara (Samalkot). Prola Raju II and Rudra Deva were Kakatiyas and Anavema Reddy a Reddi king.

s: Who is associated with building the Pancharamas or making them Shaiva kshetras?
x: Chalukya Bhima I is associated with building the Pancharamas or establishing them as Shaiva kshetras.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bhimeswara is at Draksharama. Kumararama is at Samalkot, Kumaraswamy at Chebrolu and Someswara at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram.

s: Which town was anciently called 'Chalukya Bhimavaram'?
x: Chalukya Bhimavaram is Samalkot (Kumararama), not Palakollu, which is Ksheerarama.

s: In whose memory did Chalukya Bhima I build the Kumararama temple at Samalkot?
x: Kumararama (Kumara Bhimeswara) at Samalkot was built by Chalukya Bhima I in memory of his son.

s: Where is Ksheerarama, one of the Pancharamas, located?
x: Ksheerarama is at Palakollu (West Godavari); Kumararama is at Samalkot, Amararama at Amaravati and Draksharama at Draksharama.

s: Where is Somarama, one of the Pancharamas, located?
x: Somarama is at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram; Samalkot is Bheemarama/Kumararama (Chalukya Bhimavaram) and Palakollu is Ksheerarama.

s: Which of the Pancharama temples is NOT two-storeyed?
x: All the Pancharamas except Ksheerarama are two-storeyed; the Skanda Purana and Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam are literary sources on them.

s: After the 2022 reorganisation, Amararama at Amaravati falls in which district?
x: Amararama was in Guntur district; after 2022 it is in Palnadu. Kakinada has Kumararama and Konaseema Draksharama.

s: Which is the only Pancharama on the Krishna?
x: Four Pancharamas lie in the Godavari delta; Amararama at Amaravati is on the Krishna.

s: After the 2022 reorganisation of districts, Draksharama falls in which district?
x: Draksharama, earlier in East Godavari, is now in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district.

s:
Match the following (district after 2022):
List-I (Pancharama)
A. Draksharama
B. Kumararama
C. Ksheerarama
D. Amararama
List-II (District)
1. Palnadu
2. West Godavari
3. Kakinada
4. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Draksharama - Konaseema; Kumararama (Samalkot) - Kakinada; Ksheerarama (Palakollu) - West Godavari; Amararama (Amaravati) - Palnadu.

s: Which work of Srinatha is a literary source on the Draksharama Bhimeswara temple?
x: The Skanda Purana and Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam are the literary sources on the Pancharamas.

s: Which of the twin Bhimeswara temples has a black-granite lingam in its core sanctum?
x: Samalkot (Kumararama) has a black-granite lingam; Draksharama has a massive lingam.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Draksharama and Samalkot temples:
1. Both are two-storeyed shrines built by Chalukya Bhima I.
2. The towering gopuram at Samalkot is original Eastern Chalukya work.
3. Both were renovated by the Reddis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. The Samalkot gopuram was added later, not by the Eastern Chalukyas.

s: Which Bhimeswara temple, with a huge Nandi mandapa, is one of the Trilinga kshetras?
x: Draksharama, with its huge Nandi mandapa, is one of the Trilinga kshetras.

s: What is 'Sapta Godavari' at Draksharama?
o: The sacred tank (pushkarini) of the Bhimeswara temple
A pillared mandapa built by the Reddis
A river port on the Godavari
x: Sapta Godavari is the sacred tank of the Draksharama Bhimeswara temple; its water is used for the god's abhisheka.

s: Draksharama, also known as Jananathapura, is described in the inscriptions as the coronation seat of which of the following?
x: The Draksharama inscription identifies the place as the coronation seat of a Chalukya-Chola viceroy.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 108 Shiva temples of the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: The source for this claim is the Kopparam inscription.
They were called Narendresvaralayas or Narendra Mrigeswaralayas.
One temple was built at each of his 108 battle sites.
They were built by Vijayaditya II (Narendramrigaraja).
x: The source is the Sataluru inscription; the Kopparam inscription is Pulakesin II's record. The other three statements are correct.

s: Who fought 108 fierce battles over 12 years against the Rashtrakutas and their Gangavadi allies?
x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) of the Eastern Chalukyas fought 108 battles over 12 years against the Rashtrakutas under Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I and their Gangavadi allies.

s: Which temple at Rajahmundry later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs?
x: The Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry, linked with Rajaraja Narendra like the Kotilingala and Markandeya temples, later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs.

s: Who built the Mandavya Narayana (Raja Narayana) temple at Samalkot?
x: Danarnava built the Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot; Bhattupu, commander of Chalukya Bhima I, built the Parvateswara temple at Bezawada.

s: Who built the Kumaraswamy temple at Chebrolu?
x: The Kumaraswamy temple at Chebrolu was built by Chalukya Bhima I.

s: Who built the Parvateswara temple on Indrakeeladri at Bezawada?
x: The Parvateswara temple on Indrakeeladri was built by Bhattupu, a commander of Chalukya Bhima I.

s: Who built the Kotilingala and Markandeya temples at Rajahmundry?
x: The Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu temples at Rajahmundry are linked with Rajaraja Narendra.

s: To whose time does the Bikkavolu (Biccavolu) temple group belong?
x: The Bikkavolu group belongs to Gunaga Vijayaditya's time (9th century); Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot.

s: Which is the only temple of the Bikkavolu group still standing?
x: Golingeswara is the only Bikkavolu temple still standing.

s: Which Bikkavolu temple carries carved Ganga and Yamuna figures?
x: The Vijayeswara temple at Bikkavolu has carved Ganga and Yamuna figures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bikkavolu (Biccavolu) temples?
o: Rajaraja Narendra built the Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole
The core group belongs to the 9th century
Some treat it as a Chalukya-Reddi transition group because of later Reddi additions
x: The 2025 key marked 'Rajaraja Narendra built the Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole' as incorrect; the Raja Raja temple is in Gunaga Vijayaditya's group.

s: In which region was Eastern Chalukya temple building concentrated?
x: Eastern Chalukya (Vengi school, Vesara/Chalukya style) temple building was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta.

s: Which statement correctly compares the Badami Chalukya and Vengi architectural developments?
o: The Badami Chalukyas developed Vesara in Karnataka, while the Vengi line carried a Dravida-based regional style into the Chalukya-Chola phase.
The Badami Chalukyas developed Dravida in the Krishna-Godavari delta, while the Vengi line introduced Nagara into Karnataka.
The Vengi line rejected all Badami Chalukya influence in its temple architecture.
Both dynasties developed an exclusively Buddhist style without regional variations.
x: The Badami Chalukyas developed Vesara in Karnataka, while the Vengi line transmitted a Dravida-based regional style into the Chalukya-Chola phase.

s: The Navabrahma temple complex at Alampur was constructed during the rule of which dynasty?
x: The nine Navabrahma temples at Alampur were built by the Badami Chalukyas during the 7th–8th centuries CE.

s: Which of the following temple – style pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Draksharama Bhimeswara is the model of the Chalukya-Chola (Eastern Chalukya) style, not Badami Chalukya; the other pairs are correct.

s: Eastern Chalukya temples of the Vengi School mainly followed which architectural style?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas mainly followed a Dravida-based style (Dravidian vimana), blending Pallava and Badami Chalukya influences with local Andhra features; this tradition is called the Vengi School (also described as Vesara/Chalukya).

s: Where is the Jain Ramakonda cave temple, built by Vimaladitya for his guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva?
x: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham (Vizianagaram).

s: Which of the following Jain foundation – royal patron pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vishnuvardhana III granted Mushikonda to the Jains; Nedumba Vasati was Ayyana Mahadevi's, Ramakonda Vimaladitya's and Kaluchumbarru Ammaraja II's.

s: Which was the leading Jain centre of the Eastern Chalukya period?
x: Potlacheruvu was the leading Jain centre of the period.

s: Which dynasty later took up the Telugu epigraphic practice of the Renati Cholas?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas later adopted the Telugu epigraphic practice associated with the Renati Cholas.

s: The Kalamalla inscription is associated with which ruler and date?
x: The Kalamalla inscription belongs to Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, also known as Dhanunjaya Varma, and is dated to 575 CE.

s: How many Telugu inscriptions of the Renati Cholas, mostly donation records, are known?
x: Thirty-three Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions are known, most of them donation records (dana sasanalu).

s: Between 575 and 848 CE, Telugu appeared in full prose sentences in the records of which dynasty?
x: The Renati Cholas made Telugu a royal and legislative language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit, and from 575 to 848 CE Telugu appeared in full prose sentences.

s: Before 575 CE, in what form did Telugu mainly appear in the available records?
x: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared mainly in names; complete prose sentences became characteristic from 575 to 848 CE.

s: The Renati Cholas gave Telugu its first royal dignity about how many centuries before Nannaya?
x: The Renati Cholas were the first to make Telugu a royal and legal language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit, about five centuries before Nannaya.

s: In which language are the Malepadu plates of Punyakumara, now in the Madras Museum, written?
x: The Malepadu plates of Punyakumara are in Sanskrit prose, unlike the Telugu Kalamalla record.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Renati Chola inscriptions?
o: The Kalamalla inscription is dated 575 CE.
The Malepadu plates belong to Punyakumara.
The Erragudipadu record is the first Telugu inscription of 575 CE.
The Kalamalla inscription was issued by Dhanunjaya Varma.
x: The 575 CE first Telugu inscription is Kalamalla; Erragudipadu is a separate late-6th-century stone record of Erikal Mutturaju.

s: By making Telugu a royal and legal language, the Renati Cholas replaced which languages in records?
x: The Renati Cholas were the first to make Telugu a royal and legal language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit.

s: Who issued the Erragudipadu inscription of the Renati Cholas?
x: The Erragudipadu stone record in Kamalapuram taluk belongs to Erikal Mutturaju, with a script like that of Kalamalla.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Potladurthi is associated with Renati Choda Punyakumara. Kalamalla belongs to Dhanunjaya, Satrasala to Betaraju I, and Taruvariyur to Manumasiddi I.

s: With which place were the Nellore Chodas associated?
x: The Nellore Chodas were associated with Vikrama Simhapuri; the Konidena Chodas with Kammanadu, the Pottapi Chodas with Pottapi (Kadapa) and the Renati Chodas with Renadu.

s: How did the Velanati Chodas come to an end?
o: Dhanunjaya Varma shifted the capital to Peddachapalli
Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola
x: The Velanati Choda line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Konidena Chodas ruled Kammanadu from Konidena near Narasaraopet; Pottapi was in Kadapa and Vikrama Simhapuri was the Nellore Choda seat.

s: Where did the Pottapi Chodas of Kadapa originally come from?
x: The Pottapi Chodas came from Madhurantaka and were vassals of Chola Parantaka.

s: Which was the capital of the Konidena Chodas?
x: The Konidena Chodas ruled Kammanadu from Konidena (Kotyadona) near Narasaraopet.

s: Which of the following statements about Tikkana Choda is correct?
o: He was the court poet of Manumasiddhi II and wrote Purushartha Saramu.
He ended the Velanati Choda line by killing Mummadi Rajendra Chola.
He was the founder of the Renati Chola line and ruled from Chimbapuram.
He was the son of Manumasiddhi I, helped Rajendra Chola ascend the throne and assumed the title Chola Sthapanacharya.
x: Tikkana Choda, also called Tikkabhupati, was the son of Manumasiddhi I and took the title Chola Sthapanacharya after helping Rajendra Chola ascend the throne.

s: To whom was Kavi-Brahma Tikkana minister and court poet?
x: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana was the minister and court poet of the Nellore Choda Manumasiddhi II. When Manumasiddhi II sought Kakatiya Ganapati's help against Vijayaganda Gopala, Tikkana went as envoy.

s: Against whom did Nellore Choda Manumasiddhi II seek Kakatiya Ganapati's help?
x: Manumasiddhi II sought the help of Kakatiya Ganapati against Vijayaganda Gopala.

s: Who was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas?
x: Bijjana was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas; Manumasiddhi I was their first king.

s: Who went as envoy to Kakatiya Ganapatideva when Manumasiddhi II was restored to the Nellore throne?
x: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II, with the poet Tikkana as envoy.

s: In June 2026, an ASI survey copied 25 inscriptions, including those of the Pottapi Cholas, in which tiger reserve?
x: The ASI survey in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve (Yerragondapalem) copied 25 inscriptions of the 2nd-16th centuries.

s: From whom did the Renati Cholas claim descent?
x: The Renati Cholas claimed Suryavamsa Kshatriya descent from Karikala Chola, although their culture and administration were Telugu.

s: Which was the capital of the Renati Cholas?
o: Peddachapalli, in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa
x: The principal capital was Peddachapalli in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa. Chimbapuram was specifically Dhanunjaya's capital.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dhanunjaya Varma — founder and capital at Chimbapuram
Nandivarma — last ruler and capital at Peddachapalli
Punyakumara — progenitor and title Chola Maharaja
Elachola Maharaja — founder and Kalamalla inscription
x: Dhanunjaya Varma was the founder, son of Nandivarma, and ruled from Chimbapuram. The other pairs confuse different rulers and roles.

s: For which records are the Vaidumbas particularly known?
o: Gold coins bearing only Sanskrit legends
Prakrit inscriptions from the Godavari delta
x: The Vaidumbas issued Telugu hero-stone inscriptions, also known as veerakal records.

s: Whose feudatories were the Renati Cholas at first?
x: The Renati Cholas were first feudatories of the Pallavas and later of the Badami Chalukyas; the Eastern Chalukyas only copied their Telugu inscription style.

s: Renadu, the Renati Chola territory, was called 'Saptasahasra' because it had about how many villages?
x: Renadu was known as Saptasahasra, the land of 7,000 villages.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Renati Cholas:
1. Renadu lay where the Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor regions meet.
2. Renadu lay in the upper Pennar basin.
3. Dhanunjaya Varma ruled from Peddachapalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Renadu lay in the upper Pennar basin where Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor meet; Dhanunjaya Varma's capital was Chimbapuram, while Peddachapalli was the principal capital.

s: Which dynasties succeeded the Renati Cholas?
x: The Banas and Vaidumbas came after the Renati Cholas; the Vaidumbas issued Telugu hero-stone inscriptions.

s: Who among the following was regarded as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line?
x: Nandivarma is identified as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line.

s: Who is regarded as the greatest ruler of the Renati Cholas?
x: Punyakumara (625-650 CE), with titles such as Pormukharama and Prithvivallabha, was the greatest Renati Chola ruler. Nandivarma was the progenitor, Dhanunjaya Varma the founder and Elachola Maharaja the last ruler.

s: Which of the following was NOT a title of Punyakumara?
x: Pormukharama, Purushashardula and Uttamottama were titles of Punyakumara. Chola Sthapanacharya was the title taken by Tikkana Choda.

s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Renati Chola dynasty?
x: Dhanunjaya Varma, son of Nandivarma, was the founder; Nandivarma was only the progenitor.

s: Which Renati Chola ruler bore the title 'Chola Maharaja'?
x: Satyaditya bore the title Chola Maharaja (Chola Mahadhiraju); the decline of the dynasty began after him.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Renati Cholas?
x: Elachola Maharaja was the last Renati Chola ruler.

s: Who had the title 'Muditha Silakshara Navarama'?
x: Mahendra Vikramavarman, grandson of Nandivarma and father of Punyakumara, bore this title.

s: During which period did Punyakumara, the greatest Renati Chola ruler, rule?
x: Punyakumara ruled from 625 to 650 CE.

s: Who founded the Imad Shahi dynasty of Berar, and what was its capital?
x: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk founded the Imad Shahis, whose capital was Ellichpur, also called Achalpur.

s: Which areas did Golconda acquire after the Battle of Talikota in 1565?
o: Kondavidu, Machilipatnam and the coastal districts
x: After Talikota, Golconda took Kondavidu, Machilipatnam and the coastal districts.

s: In which year did Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah found the city of Hyderabad?
x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad city in 1591; Sultan Quli founded the Golconda state in 1518 and the Charminar dates to 1594.

s: Who founded the Golconda (Hyderabad) state in 1518?
x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah founded the Golconda state in 1518 (Nizami Mosque inscription); Muhammad Quli founded Hyderabad city.

s: What was the old name of Golconda?
x: Golconda was earlier called Mankal or Mangalavaram; Mangalapura was Mangalagiri.

s: Before becoming independent in 1518, of which region was the Qutb Shahi founder the Bahmani tarafdar?
x: Sultan Quli was the Bahmani tarafdar of Telangana (1496) before becoming independent in 1518.

s: Which of the following territories was later annexed by Sultan Quli Qutb Shah in the Krishna–Godavari region?
x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah later annexed Rajahmundry, Eluru and the Krishna–Godavari region.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the contenders for the Krishna-Godavari doab and coastal Andhra?
x: The coastal dispute was among the Reddis, Velamas, Gajapatis, Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis; the Imad Shahis ruled Berar.

s: Between which rivers did the Raichur Doab lie?
x: The Raichur Doab (Raichur Antarvedi) lay between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra; it is not the Krishna-Godavari doab.

s: The Raichur Doab was the main cause of wars between which powers?
x: The fertile and strategic Raichur Doab was the main cause of the Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars, from Harihara I's time.

s: In which year was the Battle of Muttukur fought?
x: Muttukur was fought in 1263; Raichur in 1520, Rakshasi-Tangadi on 26 January 1565 and Palnadu in the 12th century.

s: Which Vijayanagara leader was killed in the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota)?
x: Aliya Rama Raya was killed at Rakshasi-Tangadi (also called Talikota or Bannihatti), fought against Golconda, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Bidar.

s: Who killed Kapaya Nayaka in the Battle of Bhimavaram (1368)?
x: At Bhimavaram in 1368 the Recherla Velamas killed Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka and gained Telangana.

s: Against whom did Krishnadevaraya fight the sieges of Kondavidu and Kondapalli (1515-16)?
x: Krishnadevaraya besieged Kondavidu and Kondapalli in 1515-16 against the Gajapatis.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: At Raichur in 1520 Krishnadevaraya defeated the Adil Shah of Bijapur; Muttukur was Ganapatideva vs Pandyas and Bhimavaram was Velamas vs Kapaya Nayaka.

s: Which of the following did NOT join the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota (1565)?
x: Golconda, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Bidar fought Vijayanagara at Talikota; Berar did not join.

s: In the battle of Devarakonda (1458), the Gajapati prince Hamvira defeated whom?
x: At Devarakonda (1458), Kapilendra's prince Hamvira defeated the Bahmanis.

s: In which year was Mahmud Gawan executed, after which the Bahmani kingdom split into five Deccan Sultanates?
x: Mahmud Gawan was executed in 1482, after which the Bahmani kingdom split into five Deccan Sultanates; 1574 is when Ahmadnagar annexed Berar.

s: In which year was the Charminar at Hyderabad constructed?
x: Hyderabad city was founded in 1591, while the Charminar was constructed in 1594.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Qutb Shahi state?
x: The Shia, Persian-using Qutb Shahi state ended under Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Saluva Dynasty was founded by Narasimha.
Hyderabad State was founded by Chin Qilich Khan, also known as Nizam-ul-Mulk.
Hyderabad City was founded by Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk.
The Tuluva Dynasty was founded by Veeranarasimha.
x: Option C is incorrect: Hyderabad City was founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591; Sultan Quli founded the Qutb Shahi dynasty itself. Saluva Narasimha, Chin Qilich Khan and Veeranarasimha are correctly matched.

s: Which Sultanate annexed Berar in 1574?
x: Berar, ruled by the Imad Shahis, was annexed by Ahmadnagar in 1574.

s: How many sultans ruled the Qutb Shahi state (1518-1687)?
x: The Qutb Shahi state lasted from 1518 to 1687 under seven sultans.

s: Who removed Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler, in 1687?
x: Aurangzeb ended the Qutb Shahi state in 1687 by removing Tana Shah.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the emergence of Deccan dynasties?
o: The Gajapatis emerged before the Bahmanis.
x: The Gajapatis emerged in 1435, well after the Bahmani kingdom (1347); the other three dates are correct.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Rudradeva declared Kakatiya independence in 1163. The other dates belong to the Gajapatis (1435), the Bahmanis (1347) and the Imad Shahis (1490).

s: The Musunuri Nayakas emerged in which period, and which rulers are associated with them?
x: The Musunuri Nayakas emerged in the 1330s and are associated with Prolaya Nayaka and Kapaya Nayaka.

s: After the Musunuri period, Prolaya Vemareddy is associated with which political formation?
x: Prolaya Vemareddy is associated with the Reddis; Singama with the Velamas, Harihara-Bukka with Vijayanagara and Hasan Gangu with the Bahmanis.

s: Which Buddhist text mentions Andhrapatha?
x: The Buddhist text Vinayavatthu mentions Andhrapatha.

s: From where did the Velamas (Recherla) rule?
x: The Recherla Velamas, founded by Singama, ruled from Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

s: Which dynasty came immediately after the Kakatiyas in the order of Andhra dynasties?
x: The Reddis (from 1325) came after the Kakatiyas, not before them.

s: Which of the following was the shift of the Kakatiya capital?
x: The Kakatiyas ruled first from Hanamkonda and then from Orugallu (Warangal).

s: Who founded the Ikshvaku dynasty of the Krishna valley?
x: Shantamula I founded the Ikshvaku dynasty; Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vijaya Deva Varma belongs to the Salankayana dynasty. Pulakeshi I is linked with the Chalukyas, Gundyana with the Kakatiyas and Prolaya Vema Reddy with the Reddy kingdom.

s: Who founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347?
x: Hasan Gangu founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347 with Gulbarga as capital.

s: Who founded the Gajapati rule of Odisha in 1435?
x: Kapilendra (1435-1467) began the Gajapati line.

s: Which were the later capitals of Vijayanagara after Hampi?
x: After Hampi, Vijayanagara ruled from Penugonda and later Chandragiri.

s: Who were the Musunuri Nayakas, Reddis and Velamas, who became independent kingdoms after 1323?
o: Three of Prataparudra's generals who survived the fall of the Kakatiyas
Three governors appointed by the Qutb Shahis
Three branches of the Imad Shahi dynasty
Three commanders of the Gajapati army
x: The Musunuri Nayakas, Reddis and Velamas were three of Prataparudra's generals who survived the Kakatiya collapse in 1323 and established independent kingdoms.

s: After which event did Kapaya Nayaka cede Golconda fort to Muhammad I of the Bahmani kingdom?
o: his capital was shifted to Kondavidu
x: Kapaya Nayaka ceded Golconda fort to Bahmani ruler Muhammad I after the death of his son Vinayaka in 1361.

s: Who shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondavidu?
x: Anavota Reddy (c. 1355) shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to the fortified Kondavidu; Prolaya Vemareddy, the founder, ruled from Addanki.

s: Which dynasty is regarded as the second unifier of all Telugu lands?
x: The Satavahanas, Kakatiyas and Qutb Shahis are regarded as the first, second and third unifiers of the Telugu lands.

s: Why is the year 1323 significant in the political history of Andhradesa?
o: The beginning of the Vijayanagara Empire in Rayalaseema
The defeat of the Gajapatis by Krishnadevaraya
The beginning of the Reddi rule in Coastal Andhra
The end of Telugu imperial unity until the Qutb Shahis reunited the region
x: The fall of the Kakatiyas in 1323 ended Telugu imperial unity; the Telugu lands stayed divided among Musunuris, Reddis, Velamas, Vijayanagara, Bahmanis and Gajapatis until the Qutb Shahis reunited the region. Vijayanagara began in 1336 and the Reddis in 1325, and Krishnadevaraya's Gajapati wars came in the 16th century.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Satavahanas were the first to unify all Telugu lands.
2. The Qutb Shahis were the third to unify all Telugu lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The unifiers of Telugu lands were the Satavahanas (first), Kakatiyas (second) and Qutb Shahis (third).

s: Who captured Kakatiya Prataparudra in 1323?
x: Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughlaq), sent by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, captured Prataparudra in 1323; Malik Kafur only made him a tributary.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate invasions of Andhra:
1. Malik Kafur's campaign of 1309-10 made Prataparudra a tributary.
2. After 1323, Warangal was renamed Sultanpur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Malik Kafur made Prataparudra a tributary in 1309-10, and after Ulugh Khan's conquest of 1323 Warangal was renamed Sultanpur.

s: In which year was the first Muslim attack on Orugallu?
x: Alauddin Khalji's army made the first attack on Orugallu in 1303; it was repulsed.

s: With whose support did the Kayasthas of the Kadapa region revolt under Ambadeva?
x: Ambadeva led the Kayastha revolt in the Kadapa region in 1272 with Pandya support.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Qutb Shahis — Bahmani governor of Telangana
Musunuri, Reddis and Velamas — Kakatiya Nayakas
x: The Kota family was subordinate to the Kakatiyas, not the Gajapatis. The Kakatiyas had earlier overlordship under the Rashtrakutas and Kalyani Chalukyas; the other pairings are correct.

s: Before becoming sovereign in 1163, whose feudatories were the Kakatiyas first?
x: The Kakatiyas served the Rashtrakutas and then the Kalyani Chalukyas before Rudradeva declared independence in 1163.

s: To whom was the Kota family, local rulers of Dharanikota, subordinate?
x: The Kota family was a Kakatiya subordinate and married Ganapatideva's daughter Ganapamba, not a Gajapati vassal.

s: In which year did the Delhi Sultanate replace the Kakatiyas at Warangal?
x: The Telangana succession ran Kakatiyas, Delhi Sultanate (1323), Musunuri Nayakas, Velamas/Bahmanis and then the Qutb Shahis.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about political succession in Coastal Andhra?
o: The Qutb Shahis came after 1565 in the later succession.
The Kakatiyas succeeded the Velanati Chodas.
The Eastern Chalukyas preceded the Velanati Chodas.
x: The Reddis succeeded the Kakatiyas, not the other way round; the other three statements are correct.

s: In Rayalaseema, who succeeded the Kakatiyas (through their Kayastha chiefs)?
x: The Rayalaseema sequence is Kakatiyas (Kayastha chiefs) → Vijayanagara → Qutb Shahis.

s: In Telangana, who followed the rule of the Delhi Sultanate (1323)?
x: The Telangana sequence is Kakatiyas → Delhi Sultanate (1323) → Musunuri Nayakas → Velamas / Bahmanis → Qutb Shahis.

s: The Palnadu war was fought in 1182 CE at which place?
x: The Palnadu war, or Palnati Yuddham, was fought at Karempudi in 1182 CE.

s: Who joined Kakatiya Rudradeva in supporting Nalagamaraju during the Palnadu conflict?
x: Kota Bhimaraju II joined Kakatiya Rudradeva to support Nalagamaraju.

s: What is the name of the epic account of the Palnadu war?
x: Srinatha’s Palnati Veera Charitra is the epic account associated with the Palnadu war.

s: In the Palnadu war, whose faction did Brahmanaidu lead?
x: Brahmanaidu led the Malideva faction; Nagamma was the minister on Nalagamaraju's side and opposed his reforms.

s: Nalagamaraju was the son of Mailama Devi. Which Velanati ruler was her father?
x: Nalagamaraju's mother Mailama Devi was the daughter of Velanati Gonka II.

s: The rival factions of the Palnadu war were all sons of which Palnadu Haihaya ruler?
x: Both factions were sons of Palnadu Haihaya Alugaraju (Anugaraju); Malideva and his brothers were Nalagamaraju's half-brothers.

s: Which community was described as having entered Palnadu as ‘intruders’ and being driven out in the Battle of Karempudi?
x: The Velamas were described as intruders into Reddi-dominated Palnadu and were driven out in the Battle of Karempudi.

s: Who was the minister of Nalagamaraju in the Palnadu war?
x: Nagamma (Nayakuralu) was Nalagamaraju's minister; Brahmanaidu led the rival Malideva faction.

s: The Palnadu war arose from the rivalry between whom?
x: The Palnadu war grew out of the rivalry of Nayakuralu Nagamma and Brahmanaidu, ministers of the two factions.

s: Who built the Veerabhadra Swamy temple at Gurajala?
x: Nagamma (Nayakuralu), Nalagama's Shaivite minister, built the Veerabhadra Swamy temple at Gurajala.

s: Which temple did Brahmanaidu open to all castes, including Dalits?
x: Brahmanaidu, a Vira Vaishnava, opened the Chennakesava temple at Macherla to all castes.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Brahmanaidu promoted inter-dining called Chapakudu.
2. Nagamma was a follower of Ramanuja's Vaishnavism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Brahmanaidu, a follower of Ramanuja, promoted Chapakudu; Nagamma was a Shaivite.

s: Who is the author of the Palnati Veera Charitra?
x: Srinatha's Palnati Veera Charitra is the epic of the Palnadu war.

s:
Assertion (A): Chapa Koodu or Dasa Samaj is associated with the Palnadu region.
Reason (R): It promoted inter-caste dining.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Brahma Naidu's Chapa Koodu belongs to Palnadu and promoted inter-caste dining, but the practice does not explain where it arose.

s: Brahma Naidu's Chennakesava temple, where Dalits were given entry, is at which place?
x: Brahma Naidu of Palnadu, founder of the Chapa Koodu (Dasa Samaj), opened the Chennakesava temple at Macherla to all.

s: Which Velanati chief was the Samasta Senadhipati of Vengi?
x: Velanati Gonka I was Samasta Senadhipati of Vengi and fought off the Kalyani Chalukyas and Kalingas.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Velanati Chodas)?
o: Areas included – Bapatla, Tenali, Repalle and Guntur
x: Mallavarma was the progenitor of the Velanati Chodas and Gonka I was the founder, so 'Founder – Mallavarma' is wrong.

s: Who was the greatest ruler of the Velanati Chodas?
x: Mallavarma was the progenitor, Gonka I the founder and Gonka II the greatest Velanati Choda.

s: Which Kakatiya ruler killed the last member of the Velanati Choda line?
x: The Velanati Choda line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed its last member, Mummadi Rajendra Choda. Earlier, the Nellore Choda Tikkana had helped Ganapati kill Prithvisvara.

s: Who were the ancestors of the Velanati Chodas?
x: The Velanati Chodas were not related to the Telugu Chodas; their ancestors were the Kirtipura lords of Madhyadesha.

s: Which was the capital of the Velanati Chodas?
x: The Velanati Chodas ruled from Chandavolu (Dhanadapuram); founder Gonka I, greatest Gonka II.

s: Which lake is named in the Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvisvara?
x: The Pithapuram inscription of the Velanati chief Prithvisvara names Kolleru Lake.

s: In which year did Kulottunga I take the Chola throne?
x: Kulottunga I took the Chola throne in 1070 and Vengi in 1075, after the death of Vijayaditya VII, the last Eastern Chalukya.

s: Who wrote the Kalingattuparani, describing Kulottunga I's conquest of Kalinga by sea?
x: Jayangondar's Kalingattuparani describes Kulottunga I's maritime conquest of Kalinga; Kulottunga I also sent 72 merchants to China and built Kulottunga Cholapuram.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Last Eastern Chalukya — Vijayaditya VII, who died in 1279
Last Eastern Chalukya — Rajaraja I, who died in 1075
x: Kulottunga I was the first Chalukya-Chola king. Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya and died in 1075, not 1279.

s: In post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra, the vassals of the nadus first accepted the overlordship of Velanadu. Whose overlordship did they accept later?
x: Post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra was a web of nadus under vassals, who accepted Velanadu and later Kakatiya overlordship when those powers were strong.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya titles did the Chalukya-Chola viceroys of Vengi assume?
x: The viceroys of Vengi took the Eastern Chalukya titles Sarvalokasraya and Sri Vishnuvardhana.

s: Kulottunga I took Vengi in 1075 after the death of the last Eastern Chalukya. Who was he?
x: Kulottunga I took Vengi in 1075 after the death of Vijayaditya VII, the last Eastern Chalukya.

s: In which role was Vikrama Chola recalled from Vengi in 1118 to serve his father?
x: Vikrama Chola, son of Kulottunga I, was recalled in 1118 to be his father's co-regent.

s: How many merchants did Kulottunga I send to China?
x: Kulottunga I sent a mission of 72 merchants to China.

s: Which town did Kulottunga I build in the Visakhapatnam region?
x: Kulottunga I built Kulottunga Cholapuram (Visakhapatnam).

s: Kulottunga I, the first Chalukya-Chola king, married Madhurantaki. Whose daughter was she?
x: Kulottunga I married Madhurantaki, daughter of the Chola Rajendra.

s: Who was the last of the Chalukya-Chola viceroy line of Vengi?
x: Parantaka Chola was the last of the viceroy line.

s: The Kona Haihayas were associated with which region and capital?
x: The Kona Haihayas ruled in Konaseema, with Rakuduru as their capital or seat.

s: With which place were the Gona Haihayas associated?
x: The Gona Haihayas were associated with Vardhamanapuram; the Palnadu Haihayas with Gurajala and the Panchadhara Haihayas with the Visakhapatnam-Yelamanchili region.

s: Who founded the Kota line, and where was its seat?
o: Bhimaraju II; Vardhamanapuram in South Telangana
x: Betaraju I was the founder of the Kota line, whose seat was Dhanyakatakam in Kammanadu.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: The Kota kings ruled Kammanadu and had Dhanyakatakam as their seat. The Vatsavayis were associated with Peddapuram, the Pusapatis with Vizianagaram, and the Bana kings with Rayalaseema and part of Karnataka.

s: From where did the Palnadu Haihayas rule?
x: The Palnadu Haihayas ruled from Gurajala; Rakuduru was the Kona Haihaya capital.

s: From where did the Chagis rule the Natavadi and Vijayavati vishayas?
x: The Chagis, raised to Mandaleswara rank by Kulottunga I, ruled from Gudimetta (later also Vinukonda).

s: From which creature did the Matsyas of Oddadi claim descent?
x: The founder of the Matsyas of Oddadi claimed descent from a fish (matsya); their emblem was a double fish.

s: Whose daughter did Satyamartanda, founder of the Matsyas of Oddadi, marry?
x: Satyamartanda married Prabhavati, daughter of Jayatsena of Utkala (Odisha), who made him ruler of the Oddadi country.

s: Which part of Andhra did the Matsyas of Oddadi rule?
x: The Matsyas of Oddadi ruled the upland Srikakulam–Vizianagaram zone of northern Andhra, near Anakapalle.

s: From whom did the Palnadu Haihayas claim descent?
x: The Palnadu Haihayas of Gurajala claimed descent from Kartavirya Arjuna.

s: Which was the capital of the Bana kings?
x: The Bana kings, who claimed descent from Bali, ruled from Parivipuram (Hindupur).

s: What was the emblem of the Matsyas of Oddadi?
x: The Matsyas of Oddadi (c. 1200-1470) had the double fish as emblem.

s: Which zamindars claim descent from the Matsyas of Oddadi?
x: After Singaraja (1471) the line was replaced by zamindaris; the Madgole zamindars claim Matsya descent.

s: A Kota chief married Ganapamba. Whose daughter was she?
x: A Kota chief married Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva; some sources name him Bhimaraju II. This marriage reflects the Kotas becoming Kakatiya vassals.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the overlords of the Kota chiefs?
o: They were first subordinate to the Chalukya-Cholas.
The Velanati Chodas followed the Chalukya-Cholas as their overlords.
The Kakatiyas were their final overlords.
The Kakatiyas were their first overlords.
x: The Kota chiefs served the Chalukya-Cholas first, then the Velanati Chodas and finally the Kakatiyas, so the Kakatiyas were the last, not the first, overlords.

s: Which Kota ruler (1108-1127) led Kalinga campaigns with the Velanati Chodas?
x: Kota Bhimaraju I (1108-1127) backed the Chalukya-Cholas and joined the Velanati Chodas in Kalinga campaigns.

s: What was the order of the overlords of the Chagi chiefs?
x: The Chagis served the Chalukya-Cholas, then the Kakatiyas, then the Gajapatis; the Velanati stage belongs to the Kota chiefs.

s: Kakatiya Ganapatideva's sister Melambika married into which family?
x: Melambika married a son of the Natavadi chief Chagi Buddharaja.

s: Where was the seat of the Pusapati family?
x: The Pusapatis ruled from Vizianagaram (APPSC GS 2022); Peddapuram was the seat of the Vatsavayis.

s: In which battle was Raja Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram killed fighting the East India Company?
x: Vijayarama Raju was killed at the Battle of Padmanabham on 10 July 1794, after which Vizianagaram became a tributary zamindari.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Pusapatis and Vatsavayis:
1. Vizianagaram was settled as a zamindari estate under the Permanent Settlement of 1802.
2. The Vatsavayis had their seat at Peddapuram.
3. The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1802.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vizianagaram became a zamindari estate in 1802 and the Vatsavayis ruled from Peddapuram; the Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.

s: Whose founder's record is the Satrasala inscription?
x: The Satrasala inscription belongs to Betaraju I, founder of the Palnadu Haihaya line at Gurajala.

s: The Taruvariyur inscription praises which ruler as a thunderbolt to his enemies?
x: The Taruvariyur inscription praises Nellore Choda Manumasiddi I as a thunderbolt to his enemies.

s: At the court of which Kalyani Chalukya ruler did Vijnaneshwara write the Mitakshara?
x: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, at the court of Vikramaditya VI.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Vikramankadevacharita was written by Bilhana. Nagavarma II wrote Kavyavalokana and Karnataka Bhashabhushana, while Basavanna was associated with Virashaiva Vachana literature.

s: Who is the author of Parashar Madhav, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti?
x: Parashar Madhav is Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti; Mitakshara is Vijnanesvara's and Chaturvarga Chintamani is Hemadri's.

s: Who is the author of the Dayabhaga?
x: Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga; Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara and Hemadri the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

s: Who is the author of the legal digest Smriti Chandrika?
x: Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika; Hemadri compiled Chaturvarga Chintamani and Ballal Sena wrote Daan Sagar.

s: Under the Dayabhaga system, when do sons acquire a right in ancestral property?
x: Dayabhaga recognises the sons' right in ancestral property only after the father's death, whereas Mitakshara gives it by birth.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Smriti Chandrika is associated with Devana Bhatta.
Parashar Madhav is associated with Devana Bhatta.
Smriti Chandrika is associated with Hindu law.
x: Option C is incorrect: Parashar Madhav is the work of Madhavacharya (Vidyaranya), not Devana Bhatta. Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika on Hindu law, and Jimutavahana wrote Dayabhaga.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mitakshara?
o: It is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti
Under it sons acquire a right in ancestral property by birth
It applied only to the upper castes
x: The claim that Mitakshara was for upper castes and Dayabhaga for lower castes is wrong; the other three statements are correct.

s: In which region does the Dayabhaga school of inheritance prevail?
x: Dayabhaga, by Jimutavahana, prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara covers most of India.

s: Who is the author of the legal work Daan Sagar?
x: Daan Sagar was written by Ballal Sena; Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika.

s: Parasara Madhaveeyam was the main law book for the administration of justice in which kingdom?
x: Madhavacharya's Parasara Madhaveeyam, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was the main law book of Vijayanagara justice.

s: On which Smriti is Madhavacharya's Parashar Madhav a commentary?
x: Parashar Madhav is a commentary on the Parashara Smriti; the Mitakshara is the commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.

s: Who is the author of the Chaturvarga Chintamani?
x: Hemadri, a minister of the Yadavas of Devagiri, wrote the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

s: The Kalyani Chalukyas flourished approximately during which period?
x: The Kalyani Chalukyas ruled from 973 CE, when Tailapa II overthrew the Rashtrakutas, to about 1189 CE, so the first option is the closest. 543–753 CE is the Badami Chalukya period.

s: Why are the Kalyani Chalukyas significant in Indian history?
o: abolished hereditary rights in ancestral property
checked Chola expansion northwards and contributed to the development of Hindu legal tradition through Mitakshara
unified all of northern India under one empire
ended the Gupta Empire and introduced Persian administration
x: The Kalyani Chalukyas checked Chola expansion towards the north, while the Mitakshara tradition associated with their court shaped Hindu inheritance law for about a millennium.

s: Which was the capital of the Kalyani Chalukyas?
x: Kalyani, now known as Basavakalyan in Karnataka, was the capital of the Kalyani Chalukyas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the broad periods of the Chalukya branches?
o: Kalyani was the earliest of the three branches
x: The order is Badami (6th–8th c.), Vengi (7th–11th c.) and Kalyani (late 10th–12th c.), so Kalyani was the latest, not the earliest.

s: Which present-day town was Kalyani, the capital of the Western Chalukyas?
x: Kalyani is present Basavakalyan in Karnataka; Badami was the earlier Chalukya capital.

s: Who among the following overthrew the last Rashtrakuta ruler Karka II in 973 CE?
x: Tailapa II overthrew the last Rashtrakuta ruler, Karka II, in 973 CE and founded the Kalyani Chalukya line.

s: Which of the following Kalyani Chalukya rulers came earliest?
x: Tailapa II preceded Satyasraya, who was followed by Someshvara I and later Vikramaditya VI.

s: The Kalyani Chalukya Someshvara I granted Hanamkonda to which Kakatiya chief?
x: Someshvara I granted Hanamkonda to Kakatiya Prola I; he also killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam and took the title Vengi Purveshwara.

s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler bore the title Tribhuvanamalla and ruled for 50 years?
x: Vikramaditya VI, the greatest Kalyani Chalukya ruler, ruled for 50 years as Tribhuvanamalla and brought the Vengi feudatories under his control.

s: Which of the following is correct about the Chalukya-Vikrama era?
o: started by Someshvara III in 1126 CE to commemorate Manasollasa
founded by Tailapa II in 973 CE after defeating the Rashtrakutas
introduced by Someshvara I after the battle of Koppam in 1053 CE
founded by Vikramaditya VI in 1076 CE and used in place of the Saka era in royal records
x: Vikramaditya VI founded the Chalukya-Vikrama era in 1076 CE, the year of his accession, replacing the Saka era in royal records.

s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler took the title 'Vengi Purveshwara' after the battle of Koppam?
x: Someshvara I Ahavamalla took the title Vengi Purveshwara after killing Rajadhiraja I at Koppam (1053).

s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi in 1006 CE?
x: Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi in 1006; he was repulsed by Saktivarman I with Chola help.

s: During which period did Someshvara I Ahavamalla rule?
